documents.title: Evaluating LLMs as a Bridge Between Cyber Threats and Business Risk (page 15)
documents.snippet: le-report disagreement Figure 3: Analyst vs. AI-Instrument Validation (N = 60 Dual-Scored Reports) The AI instrument and author agreed on pass/fail verdicts in only 38.3% of the 60 dual- scored reports, representing a 61.7% verdict-flip rate. The mean absolute composite divergence of 0.517 points represents a large difference given the 1.0 to 5.0 scale, and the maximum single- report divergence of 1.555 points indicates that individual report quality assessments can differ substantially between both rating systems. documents.title: Evaluating LLMs as a Bridge Between Cyber Threats and Business Risk (page 20)
documents.snippet: nfiguration, produced a 1.5% pass rate on the same rubric, a spread of nearly 72 percentage points. More consequentially, the author validation exercise revealed a 61.7% verdict-flip rate and a mean absolute composite divergence of 0.517 across 60 dual-scored reports, indicating that the AI scoring instrument used in this study systematically overestimated report quality. The actual pass rates under human expert judgment are likely substantially lower than the primary findings report, and the Language Appropriateness dimension, the highest performing under AI scoring, exhibited the greatest divergence from human assessment. documents.title: Evaluating LLMs as a Bridge Between Cyber Threats and Business Risk (page 19)
documents.snippet: Evaluating LLMs as a Bridge Between Cyber Threats and Business Risk 19 Arcadio Aguilar, aggie0222@gmail.com documented in the inter-rater validation establish that the AI-instrument pass rates reported here are at most upper-bound estimates. Full re-scoring of the 1,000-report dataset by at least two independent CTI-qualified evaluators using agreement metrics is a prerequisite for the pass rate findings to serve as reliable benchmarks. A calibration exercise using 30 to 50 reports with defined scoring examples per dimension would substantially reduce rater drift before a greater scoring effort begins. documents.title: Evaluating LLMs as a Bridge Between Cyber Threats and Business Risk (page 9)
documents.snippet: ompt configuration achieves a 73.5% pass rate, while the least effective achieves a 1.5% pass rate. A subsequent human-analyst inter-rater exercise revealed a 61.7% verdict-flip rate across 60 dual-scored reports, establishing that the AI scoring instrument overestimated quality in a significant proportion of cases. The findings establish that model capability alone is neither the limiting factor nor the reliable determinant of output quality. 3.1 Overall Performance and Aggregate Findings Of the 1,000 AI-generated reports scored against the four-dimension composite rubric, 388 (38.8%) met or exceeded the ≥3.5 quality threshold under AI-instrument scoring.
